content:
mike: Heads-up — after the v0.24.1 rollout we started seeing memory climb on our long-context perf harnesses, a few OOMs in prod, and retention in the kv cache that never drops.

sara: saw that in the alerting dashboard, mem-usage on `inference-pool-3` jumped from ~18GB to ~42GB over 6 hours. no spikes in qps.

cheng: I ran `pmap` + `smem` on a repro box. Private heap grew, RSS increased but `pss` indicates retained arena size. jemalloc stats show retained: 22GB, active: 40GB.

alyssa: did we change any eviction logic recently? I vaguely remember the batching hysteresis PR touching cache window lifetime.

mike: yes — PR 3a7f9b2 changed the eviction hysteresis to prefer larger batches (to reduce kernel churn). It also adjusted the kv-slot LRU threshold. That landed in yesterday's merge.

perf-ci: CI perf job `longctx-memory` failed on post-merge check: peak-RSS +65% vs baseline, test id 2026-03-18T02.

cheng: bisected locally: revert of commit `3a7f9b2` stops the growth. Patch `revert-3a7f9b2` reduces retained to baseline. So the hysteresis change is the main suspect.

mike: interesting — how does batching hysteresis cause kv retention?

cheng: hypothesis: hysteresis increased average batch latencies, which changed sequence-length distribution seen by kernel-selection heuristics, so the runtime routes more requests to a different kernel variant that keeps larger KV entries around (larger attention caches), and eviction path isn't triggering because of the new LRU threshold. Combined effect: slower eviction + larger per-item size.

alyssa: can you paste the small profiler dump? especially top allocation sites and kv cache stats.

cheng: profiler (sampling, 30s):
```
Top alloc callers:
  34.2%  runtime::kv::store::insert
  22.8%  runtime::attention::kv_store_alloc
  11.0%  runtime::batch::assemble
  6.5%   runtime::kernel_selector::select_variant
```
kv stats endpoint `/debug/kv`: `items=14321, evictable=210, total_bytes=18_342_112_000, avg_item=1_280_000`

mike: avg_item looks huge — 1.28MB per entry suggests large cached KVs for long contexts. Were we landing a new kernel that stores full float32 KV instead of quantized keys?

cheng: yes — the kernel-selection diff changed preferred quantization path for sequence lengths > 4k. For longctx we ended up in the float path. commit `b6d4f1c` (in same merge set) changed the fallback order.

sara: so it's not purely eviction config; it's interaction between kernel-selection and batching heuristics. That's nasty.

alyssa: did we get any mmap growth logs? I saw `munmap` not called on slab shrink in dmesg on one box.

cheng: confirmed: arena shrink didn't release to OS. jemalloc retained memory because arena fragmentation increased — pages are free inside allocator but not returned. Reverting 3a7f9b2 drops fragmentation.

mike: action plan?

cheng: immediate: revert PR 3a7f9b2 in prod (we have a quick revert candidate). Then run canary longctx harness and watch retained bytes + kv metrics for a few hours.

alyssa: medium: add a guard in kernel-selection to avoid switching to full-float KV for unverified workloads, and add an explicit eviction waterline that forces compaction when retained > X.

mike: long: add a perf CI test for kv retained over longctx with sequence-len distribution and make the post-merge job block merges if retained > 10% above baseline.

perf-ci: I can wire the gating rule. failing job: https://ci.redwood.ai/longctx-memory/2026-03-18/failed

mike: who will revert and monitor?

cheng: I'll push revert now: `git revert -m 1 3a7f9b2 && git push prod-revert` and open rollback PR.

alyssa: I'll prepare the kernel-selection guard patch and a small eviction override feature flag so we can test without blocking rollouts.

sara: I'll run the canary tests and hook the alerting thresholds to the retention metric.

deploy-bot: Deploy started for `revert-3a7f9b2` to canary (inference-pool-1).

mike: thanks. once canary is stable for 2h we'll promote. Also add a follow-up to instrument per-item quantization-path in `/metrics` to make future debugging easier.

cheng: noted — will add `kv_quant_path` label to metrics and a perf regression test for float vs quantized memory footprints.

alyssa: also filing an RFC to formalize interactions between batching heuristics and kernel selection; these cross-cutting tweaks keep biting us.

mike: nice. keep updates here. if revert doesn't fix it we'll bisect the other commit in the merge set (`b6d4f1c`).
